items.name: Qwen4-Max
items.plain: Alibaba's new flagship AI for long documents, coding and agent work, now available to businesses through its cloud API.
items.summary: Alibaba's first Qwen4 model, Qwen4-Max, went generally available on November 16 after a two-week preview, bringing multimodal text, image and video understanding with a 1M-token context to its cloud API and apps.

items.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.plain: A fast open-weight AI for long coding and document jobs, now runnable inside AWS with enterprise controls.
items.summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed is now available on Amazon Bedrock: a post-trained version of the open-weight Kimi K3 flagship, tuned for long-horizon agent work, coding and documents, with prompts kept inside the AWS data boundary.

items.name: MiniMax H3-Image
items.plain: An image model that creates and edits print-quality visuals from text or reference photos, ready to run in-house or via API.
items.summary: MiniMax released H3-Image on November 10, an open-weight image model that generates and edits native 4K images in about 10 seconds, handling text-to-image and edits from up to 16 reference images in a single checkpoint.

items.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
items.plain: Google's most capable AI for long, complex work such as security analysis and software engineering, now open to paying customers.
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available on November 10: its strongest Gemini 4 model, built for cybersecurity work and long-horizon agentic workflows, now open to developers, enterprises and AI Ultra subscribers.

items.name: Ling-3.2-flash
items.plain: Ant's new AI that understands text, images and video together, useful for document and agent work, free to try for two weeks.
items.summary: Ant Ling launched Ling-3.2-flash on November 5, its first native multimodal model, reading text, images and video for visual understanding, long-horizon agent work and medical analysis, free via API for its first two weeks.
